findings.text: The report has no dedicated safety benchmark table for the released model; safety appears only in supervised fine-tuning (SFT)/reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) data construction and a Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) tool-hallucination ablation.

source.quote:

findings.text: The authors state the released model does not use DPO for tool-hallucination control because reinforcement learning (RL) already matched that performance.

our released model does not rely on DPO, because reinforcement learning (RL) already achieved

findings.text: SFT safety responses are filtered with a content-safety classifier before training.

source.quote:
A content-safety classifier is employed to filter the responses, ensuring alignment with
safety objectives.

findings.text: RLHF safety preference data labels harmful prompts as safe-vs-unsafe and safe prompts as safe-vs-over-refusal.

source.quote:
for harmful
prompts, <safe, unsafe> completions are labeled as the <chosen, rejected> pairs. For safe prompts,
<safe, over-refusal> completions are annotated similarly as <chosen, rejected> pairs.

notes: Technical report (arXiv:2512.20848), not a system card. No risk framework, external safety testers, or safety benchmark scores for the released checkpoint. Only numeric safety-purpose results are tool hallucination rates in Table 7 (DPO ablation; released model uses RL instead). Capability tables skipped per pilot (name in reply): Table 2/3/4/5/6/8 and Figure 1 (MMLU-Pro, AIME25 accuracy, GPQA accuracy, LiveCodeBench, SciCode, HLE, MiniF2F, Terminal Bench, SWE-Bench, TauBench, BFCL, IFBench, Scale AI Multi Challenge, Arena-Hard-V2, AA-LCR, RULER, MMLU-ProX, WMT24++, MMLU-redux, prompt sensitivity).
